Theorem
[A priori criterion for Dirichlet solvability] Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0293, gilbarg-trudinger:page-0294 ↗ gt-thm-11-3 1. ch11:11.4\group gt-ch11

Let $\partial \Omega \in C^{2,\alpha }$, $\varphi \in C^{2,\alpha }(\overline\Omega )$, and suppose $Q$ is elliptic on $\overline\Omega $ with $a^{ij},b\in C^1$ on $\overline\Omega \times \mathbb R\times \mathbb R^n$. If for some $\beta >0$ every $C^{2,\alpha }$ solution of (11.5), uniformly in $\sigma \in [0,1]$, satisfies \begin{equation} \tag {11.6} \| u\| _{C^{1,\beta }(\overline\Omega )}<M, \end{equation} then $Qu=0$ with $u=\varphi $ on $\partial \Omega $ has a solution in $C^{2,\alpha }(\overline\Omega )$.
Proof

↗ gt-thm-11-4 \sketch Linear Schauder theory makes the operator in (11.4) well defined. The global estimate maps bounded subsets of $C^{1,\beta }$ to bounded subsets of $C^{2,\alpha \beta }$, hence to precompact subsets of $C^{1,\beta }$. Passing to the limit in (11.4) proves continuity. Theorem 1 and (11.6) therefore give a fixed point; Schauder regularity improves it to $C^{2,\alpha }$.
